evidence_excerpts: If such additional facts are available, we have reason to believe that D is a mere partial ground that was misidentified as a full ground; in such a case, [p] instead is fully grounded in D, P.

additional explanatorily relevant facts are available that meet the modal entailment condition: what are identified as enabling conditions in the first case, a totality fact ... in the second case, and the fact that Socrates and Xanthippe were married in the third case.
text: Putative counterexamples involving promises, universal generalizations, and widowhood fail when merely partial grounds are supplemented by additional explanatorily relevant facts that restore modal entailment.
